items.title: Vanilla Birthday Layer Cake
items.subtitle: snack · 1 slice (1/16 of the cake), unfrosted
items.body: A tender, buttery two-layer vanilla cake, the classic birthday cake. Frost it with vanilla or chocolate buttercream.

items.title: Chocolate Birthday Layer Cake
items.subtitle: snack · 1 slice (1/16 of the cake), unfrosted
items.body: A dark, moist one-bowl chocolate cake made with cocoa, oil and hot water. No mixer needed.

items.title: Vanilla Sheet Cake for a Crowd
items.subtitle: snack · 1 square (1/24 of a half-sheet), unfrosted
items.body: One big, flat vanilla cake for a class or a crowd. Frost it right in the pan; no stacking or leveling.

items.title: Chocolate Sheet Cake with Fudge Frosting
items.subtitle: snack · 1 square, frosted
items.body: A thin, fudgy chocolate cake in a half-sheet pan, with a glossy cocoa frosting poured over while it’s warm. Feeds a crowd, ready in about an hour.

items.title: Vanilla Cupcakes
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cupcake, unfrosted
items.body: Soft vanilla cupcakes, 24 to a batch. Easy to carry to school, easy to hand out, no slicing.

items.title: Chocolate Cupcakes
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cupcake, unfrosted
items.body: Moist one-bowl chocolate cupcakes made with cocoa and oil. They stay soft for days.

items.title: Egg-Free, Dairy-Free Chocolate Cake (Wacky Cake)
items.subtitle: snack · 1 square (1/9 of an 8-inch cake)
items.body: The old “wacky cake”: no eggs, milk or butter, mixed right in the pan, risen with baking soda and vinegar. Handy when a guest can’t have eggs or dairy.

items.title: Vanilla Buttercream
items.subtitle: snack · about 3 tablespoons (makes about 3½ cups)
items.body: Fluffy American buttercream: butter beaten with powdered sugar, cream and vanilla. Enough to fill and frost a two-layer cake or 24 cupcakes.

items.title: Chocolate Buttercream
items.subtitle: snack · about 3 tablespoons (makes about 3½ cups)
items.body: Creamy cocoa buttercream for filling and frosting a two-layer cake or 24 cupcakes.

items.title: Cream Cheese Frosting
items.subtitle: snack · about 3 tablespoons (makes about 3 cups)
items.body: Tangy, smooth frosting for chocolate, vanilla or carrot cake. A cake frosted with it lives in the refrigerator.

items.title: Hot Fudge Sauce (and a Sundae Bar)
items.subtitle: snack · 2 tablespoons (makes about 1½ cups)
items.body: Thick, glossy chocolate sauce in 10 minutes, for an ice cream sundae bar at the party or a scoop next to the cake.

items.title: Make-Your-Own Mini Pizzas
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 2 mini pizzas
items.body: English muffin halves the guests top themselves with sauce, cheese and toppings. A party activity and lunch in one.

items.title: Party Pigs in a Blanket
items.subtitle: snack · 3 pieces (makes 24)
items.body: Little pieces of hot dog wrapped in biscuit dough and baked golden. The snack that disappears first.

ingredients.prep: refrigerated biscuits, each cut in 3 strips

items.title: Crispy Baked Chicken Tenders
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 3 tenders
items.body: Chicken tenders coated in Parmesan panko and baked until crunchy. Everyone’s party favorite, without frying.

items.title: Baked Ham and Cheese Party Sliders
items.subtitle: lunch,snack · 1 slider
items.body: A whole tray of soft sweet rolls filled with ham and Swiss, brushed with butter and mustard and baked until melty.

items.title: Veggie Cups with Ranch Dip
items.subtitle: snack,side · 1 cup
items.body: Each guest gets a cup with ranch in the bottom and vegetable sticks standing up in it. No double-dipping, and it looks bright on the table.

items.title: Fresh-Squeezed Party Lemonade
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cup
items.body: Real lemonade from fresh lemons and a simple syrup, a gallon pitcher for the party. Not too sweet; add more syrup to taste.

items.title: Foil-Packet Hamburger Dinners
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 packet
items.body: The classic campfire supper: a seasoned beef patty on sliced potatoes, carrots and onion, sealed in foil and cooked in the coals.

items.title: Foil-Packet Italian Chicken and Vegetables
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 packet
items.body: Chunks of chicken with zucchini, peppers and onion, olive oil and Italian herbs, cooked in foil packets over the coals.

items.title: Foil-Packet Sausage, Potatoes and Corn
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 packet
items.body: Smoked sausage, little potatoes, corn on the cob and green beans with butter and paprika. Like a shrimp boil without the pot.

items.title: Campfire Banana Boats
items.subtitle: snack · 1 banana
items.body: A banana split in its peel, stuffed with chocolate chips and marshmallows and warmed in the coals until gooey. Eat it with a spoon.

ingredients.prep: cut in half, or 1 cup minis

items.title: Campfire Dutch-Oven Chili
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1½ cups
items.body: A big pot of beef and bean chili, simmered over the fire or a camp stove. Warms everyone up on a cool night.

items.title: Camp Skillet Breakfast Hash
items.subtitle: breakfast · about 1½ cups with 2 eggs
items.body: Bacon, crispy hash browns, peppers and onion in one big skillet, with eggs cooked right on top. Breakfast for the whole campsite.

ingredients.prep: kept in the cooler; thawed is fine

items.title: Shake-and-Pour Camp Pancakes
items.subtitle: breakfast · 3 pancakes
items.body: Mix the dry ingredients at home in a bottle with powdered milk. At camp, add water and oil, shake, and pour. No eggs to keep cold.

items.title: Dutch-Oven Peach Cobbler
items.subtitle: snack · about ¾ cup
items.body: Canned peaches under a buttery batter, baked in a Dutch oven with coals underneath and on the lid. The classic campout dessert.

ingredients.prep: in juice, drained (save ½ cup juice)

items.title: Campfire Bannock (Skillet or Stick)
items.subtitle: side,breakfast · 1 wedge
items.body: A simple flatbread of flour, baking powder, fat and water, cooked in a skillet or wrapped around a stick over the coals. A camp staple for centuries.

items.title: Walking Tacos
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 bag of chips with toppings
items.body: Taco meat spooned straight into a bag of tortilla chips, topped and eaten with a fork. Hardly any dishes to wash at camp.

ingredients.prep: in 6 single-serving bags or zip-top bags

items.title: Pie-Iron Pizza Pockets
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 1 pocket
items.body: Buttered bread around pizza sauce, mozzarella and pepperoni, toasted in a pie iron over the coals until crisp and melty.

items.title: One-Pot Camp Stove Mac and Cheese
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1¼ cups
items.body: Macaroni cooked in just enough water to soak up, then stirred with milk, butter and cheddar. One pot, no draining.

items.title: Cinnamon Sugar Biscuits on a Stick
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 1 twist
items.body: Biscuit dough twisted around a roasting stick, toasted over the coals, then rolled in butter and cinnamon sugar.

items.title: Nut-Free Camp Trail Mix
items.subtitle: snack · ½ cup
items.body: Seeds, oat cereal, pretzels, raisins, cranberries and a few chocolate chips. All the crunch of trail mix, without peanuts or tree nuts.

items.title: Homemade Hot Cocoa Mix
items.subtitle: snack · ⅓ cup mix (1 mug)
items.body: Powdered milk, cocoa and sugar mixed at home. At camp, stir a scoop into a mug of hot water for cocoa by the fire.

items.title: Sugar Cookie Cutouts with Royal Icing
items.subtitle: snack · 1 iced cookie (about 3 inches)
items.body: Buttery cutouts that hold their shape in the oven, iced with smooth royal icing that dries hard enough to stack. The cookie most people picture for decorating day.

items.title: Gingerbread People
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cookie (about 4 inches)
items.body: Dark, spicy molasses cookies, soft in the middle with crisp edges. Decorate with royal icing buttons and smiles.

items.title: Gingerbread House
items.subtitle: snack · 1 piece when you break it up (it’s mostly for looking at)
items.body: A sturdy construction gingerbread, baked flat and hard, glued together with stiff royal icing and covered in candy. A family project for a December weekend.

items.title: Scottish-Style Butter Shortbread
items.subtitle: snack · 1 finger
items.body: Three main ingredients, butter, sugar and flour, pressed into a pan and baked low and slow until pale gold and sandy-crisp. Keeps for weeks and packs well for gifts.

ingredients.prep: or rice flour, for extra tenderness

items.title: Snickerdoodles
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cookie
items.body: Soft, crackly cookies rolled in cinnamon sugar. Cream of tartar gives them their slight tang and pillowy middle.

items.title: Jam Thumbprint Cookies
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cookie
items.body: Tender butter cookies with a thumb-pressed well of bright jam. Use raspberry and apricot for a red-and-gold tray.

items.title: Spritz Butter Cookies
items.subtitle: snack · 2 small cookies
items.body: Little pressed butter cookies in wreaths, trees and flowers. Their name comes from the German word for “to squirt,” which is what the press does.

ingredients.prep: or 1 teaspoon vanilla and ½ teaspoon almond extract

items.title: Chocolate Crinkle Cookies
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cookie
items.body: Fudgy cocoa cookies rolled in powdered sugar that cracks into a snowy pattern as they bake.

items.title: Peppermint Bark
items.subtitle: snack · 1 piece (about 1 oz)
items.body: A layer of dark chocolate, a layer of white chocolate and a shower of crushed candy canes. No baking, and it makes a pretty gift.

items.title: Easy Chocolate Fudge
items.subtitle: snack · 1 square (about 1¼ inches)
items.body: Smooth, rich fudge from chocolate chips and sweetened condensed milk, with no candy thermometer needed. Add nuts if your family eats them.

items.title: Standing Rib Roast (Prime Rib)
items.subtitle: dinner · about ⅔ lb as bought (one thick slice)
items.body: A bone-in beef rib roast with a garlic, herb and black-pepper crust, roasted at 325°F the USDA way. The bones make their own rack and the drippings make the Yorkshire puddings.

items.title: Yorkshire Puddings
items.subtitle: side · 1 pudding
items.body: Tall, crisp, hollow puddings baked in sizzling beef drippings. The classic partner for roast beef, from northern England.

ingredients.prep: beef drippings from the roast, or vegetable oil

items.title: Horseradish Cream Sauce
items.subtitle: side · about 2 tablespoons
items.body: Cool sour cream with a sharp bite of horseradish and a little lemon. The sauce for prime rib.

items.title: Beef Pan Gravy
items.subtitle: side · about ¼ cup
items.body: A smooth brown gravy made from the roast’s drippings and beef broth while the meat rests.

ingredients.prep: fat from the roast's drippings, or butter

items.title: Extra-Crisp Roast Potatoes
items.subtitle: side · about 1 cup
items.body: Potatoes boiled until just tender, shaken in the colander to rough up their edges, then roasted in hot fat until glassy-crisp outside and fluffy inside.

ingredients.prep: or Yukon-type, peeled and cut in 2-inch chunks
for the cooking water (most is poured away)
or beef drippings, duck fat or lard

items.title: Honey-Roasted Carrots and Parsnips
items.subtitle: side · about ¾ cup
items.body: Sweet root vegetables roasted until caramelized, then tossed with honey and thyme. A classic on British and American holiday tables.

ingredients.prep: peeled, halved lengthwise and cut in 3-inch sticks
peeled, cut like the carrots (core removed if woody)

items.title: Berry and Custard Trifle
items.subtitle: snack · about 1 cup
items.body: Layers of soft sponge cake, raspberry jam, berries, homemade vanilla custard and whipped cream in a glass bowl. A British Christmas classic, made family-style with orange juice instead of sherry.

ingredients.prep: fresh or thawed frozen, plus strawberries

items.title: Bûche de Noël (Yule Log Cake)
items.subtitle: snack · 1 slice
items.body: A rolled chocolate sponge filled with whipped cream and frosted with chocolate ganache scored to look like bark. Paris pastry shops made the log famous in the late 1800s.

items.title: Christmas Morning Sausage Strata
items.subtitle: breakfast · 1 square
items.body: Bread, browned sausage, cheese and eggs assembled the night before. In the morning it goes straight into the oven while presents are opened.

ingredients.prep: bulk, or links removed from casings

items.title: Béchamel Sauce
items.subtitle: side · ¼ cup (makes 2 cups)
items.body: Escoffier’s white sauce: milk thickened with a butter-and-flour roux and simmered with onion and bay. The base for mac and cheese, lasagna and creamed vegetables.

items.title: Chicken Velouté
items.subtitle: side · ¼ cup (makes 2 cups)
items.body: A silky sauce of good chicken stock thickened with a pale roux and skimmed as it simmers. Spoon it over chicken, fish or vegetables, or use it to start a pot pie.

ingredients.prep: more if the stock is unsalted

items.title: Espagnole and Demi-Glace (Brown Sauce)
items.subtitle: side · ¼ cup (makes 2 cups)
items.body: Escoffier’s brown sauce: brown stock, a browned roux, vegetables, bacon and tomato, simmered and skimmed. Reduce it with more stock and it becomes demi-glace, the base of steak sauces.

ingredients.prep: homemade brown stock is best, unsalted

items.title: Escoffier’s Tomato Sauce
items.subtitle: side · ½ cup (makes about 6 cups)
items.body: The French classic tomato sauce: bacon, carrot and onion, a little flour, tomatoes and stock, cooked slowly in the oven, then passed through a sieve. Smooth, rich and mild.

ingredients.prep: 28-oz cans, with juice, crushed by hand (or 5 lb ripe tomatoes, chopped)

items.title: Hollandaise Sauce
items.subtitle: side · about 3 tablespoons
items.body: Egg yolks whisked over gentle heat until thick, then beaten with warm butter and lemon. Rich and tangy, for eggs Benedict, asparagus and fish.

items.title: Peach Melba
items.subtitle: snack · 1 peach with ice cream and sauce
items.body: Escoffier’s famous dessert: peaches poached in vanilla syrup, served on vanilla ice cream under a fresh raspberry purée.

items.title: Pears Belle-Hélène
items.subtitle: snack · 1 pear with ice cream and sauce
items.body: Pears poached in vanilla syrup, chilled, and served on vanilla ice cream with hot chocolate sauce poured over at the table.

items.title: Crêpes Suzette
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 3 crêpes
items.body: Thin crêpes warmed in a buttery orange sauce. Escoffier’s 1907 version brushes them with orange butter; ours makes it a glossy pan sauce, with no liqueur and no flames.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus a little for the pan
or the juice of clementines or tangerines

items.title: Melba Toast
items.subtitle: snack,side · 4 crisp halves
items.body: Toast split into paper-thin slices and baked until crisp and curled. A light partner for soup, pâté or cheese.

items.title: Potato and Leek Soup (Potage Parmentier)
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 1⅓ cups
items.body: Leeks softened in butter, simmered with potatoes and stock, puréed and finished with cream. Escoffier topped it with butter-fried croutons.

ingredients.prep: white and light green parts, sliced and well rinsed

items.title: Hunter’s Chicken (Chicken Chasseur)
items.subtitle: dinner · 2 thighs with sauce
items.body: Chicken browned in butter and oil, then finished in a sauce of mushrooms, shallots, tomato and parsley. A classic French bistro dinner.

items.title: Fish Bonne Femme
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 fillet with sauce
items.body: White fish fillets poached on a bed of shallots and mushrooms, then coated with the pan juices made into a creamy sauce. Escoffier’s “good wife’s” sole, for any mild white fish.

ingredients.prep: about 6 oz each, or sole, flounder or tilapia

items.title: Lobster Newberg
items.subtitle: dinner · about ¾ cup on toast
items.body: Cooked lobster warmed in butter, simmered in cream, and thickened with egg yolks and a pinch of cayenne. Delmonico’s showpiece, served on toast.

ingredients.prep: toasted and cut in triangles, or 2 cups cooked rice

items.title: Eggs Benedict
items.subtitle: breakfast · 2 halves
items.body: Toasted English muffins topped with ham, a poached egg and hollandaise. Delmonico’s chef printed it in 1894 as “Eggs à la Benedick.”

ingredients.prep: thick-sliced cooked ham or Canadian bacon

items.title: Baked Alaska
items.subtitle: snack · 1 wedge
items.body: Ice cream on sponge cake, sealed in meringue and browned in a very hot oven for just a few minutes. Delmonico’s “Alaska, Florida”: cold inside, warm outside.

ingredients.prep: from pasteurized eggs, or carton whites labeled for whipping

items.title: Delmonico Steak with Parsley Butter
items.subtitle: dinner · about 5 oz of steak
items.body: A thick sirloin steak, salted, brushed with butter and broiled, served with lemony parsley butter. Ranhofer’s plain steak, the way Delmonico’s served it.

items.title: The Original Waldorf Salad (1896)
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about ¾ cup
items.body: The Waldorf’s first version: just apples and celery in mayonnaise. Walnuts and grapes came later.

ingredients.prep: crisp and tart-sweet, peeled and cored

items.title: Celery Victor
items.subtitle: side · about 4 oz of celery
items.body: Celery hearts simmered in stock, cooled in it, and dressed with oil, vinegar and herbs. A cool, savory salad from San Francisco’s Hotel St. Francis.

ingredients.prep: the pale inner stalks (hearts) of 2 bunches, halved lengthwise
or chicken broth, closer to the original

items.title: Delmonico Potatoes
items.subtitle: side · about ⅔ cup
items.body: Diced potatoes simmered in cream, topped with Parmesan and baked until golden. The St. Francis version of a Delmonico’s favorite.

ingredients.prep: or 1 cup cream and ½ cup milk

items.title: Grilled Hot Dogs with All the Toppings
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 hot dog in a bun, with toppings
items.body: Hot dogs grilled until they blister, in toasted buns, with a toppings bar so everyone builds their own: mustard, ketchup, relish, onions, sauerkraut and cheese.

items.title: Grilled Barbecue Chicken
items.subtitle: dinner · 2 pieces
items.body: Bone-in thighs and drumsticks cooked over gentle heat until tender, then brushed with barbecue sauce at the end so it turns sticky instead of burning.

items.title: Lemon-Herb Grilled Chicken Breasts
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 breast half (about 5 oz cooked)
items.body: Chicken breasts pounded to an even thickness and marinated in lemon, garlic, oregano and olive oil, so they grill fast and stay juicy. Good hot, or sliced cold onto salads.

items.title: Grill-Smoked Baby Back Ribs
items.subtitle: dinner · about ⅓ rack
items.body: Two racks of ribs cooked low and slow beside the fire, not over it, then wrapped to turn tender and brushed with sauce at the end. A cookout afternoon project.

items.title: Grilled Vegetable Skewers
items.subtitle: side,dinner · 2 skewers
items.body: Zucchini, peppers, red onion, mushrooms and cherry tomatoes tossed in garlic and herbs and grilled until charred at the edges. A side for everyone, and a main for vegetarians.

items.title: Classic Mustard Potato Salad
items.subtitle: side · about ⅔ cup
items.body: The yellow, old-fashioned kind: tender potatoes dressed while warm with vinegar, then mixed with mayonnaise, mustard, pickles, celery, onion and chopped egg.

ingredients.prep: for the cooking water (most drains away)

items.title: Picnic Macaroni Salad
items.subtitle: side · about ⅔ cup
items.body: Elbow macaroni in a creamy, tangy dressing with crunchy celery, bell pepper and a little sweet pickle. A cookout classic kids reach for.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most drains away)

items.title: Homemade Baked Beans with Bacon
items.subtitle: side · about ½ cup
items.body: Navy beans baked slowly with bacon, onion, molasses, brown sugar and mustard until the sauce turns thick and glossy. Made from canned beans, so no overnight soak.

ingredients.prep: navy or great northern, 15 oz each, drained and rinsed

items.title: Tangy Vinegar Coleslaw
items.subtitle: side · about ¾ cup
items.body: A crunchy, mayonnaise-free slaw dressed with cider vinegar, a little sugar and celery seed. It holds up better than creamy slaw on a hot day and belongs on a pulled pork sandwich.

ingredients.prep: about 2 lb, cored and thinly sliced, or 2 bags coleslaw mix

items.title: Grilled Street-Style Corn
items.subtitle: side · 1 ear
items.body: Corn grilled until charred, then coated with a creamy lime sauce, crumbled cheese and chili powder, in the style of Mexican elote sold by street vendors.

items.title: Homemade Barbecue Sauce
items.subtitle: side · 2 tablespoons (makes about 2 cups)
items.body: A sweet, tangy, lightly smoky sauce from ketchup, molasses, vinegar and spices. Twenty minutes on the stove, and it keeps for weeks.

items.title: Fresh-Squeezed Lemonade
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cup
items.body: Real lemons, sugar dissolved into a quick syrup so it never sits gritty at the bottom, and cold water. Easy to make less sweet, or pink with berries.

ingredients.prep: juiced, for about 1½ cups juice (or 1½ cups bottled lemon juice)

items.title: Flag Sheet Cake with Berries
items.subtitle: snack · 1 piece (1/20 of a 9x13 cake)
items.body: A tender vanilla sheet cake spread with a light cream cheese whipped frosting, with blueberries in the corner and rows of raspberries or strawberries for stripes.

items.title: Strawberry Shortcakes
items.subtitle: snack · 1 shortcake with berries and cream
items.body: Tender, lightly sweet biscuits split and piled with juicy sugared strawberries and softly whipped cream. A summer dessert that tastes best the day you make it.

items.title: Red, White and Blue Yogurt Parfaits
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 1 parfait (about 1 cup)
items.body: Layers of vanilla yogurt, strawberries, blueberries and crunchy granola in clear cups. No oven, and kids can make them.

ingredients.prep: or plain Greek yogurt with honey

items.title: Sweet Noodle Kugel
items.subtitle: side,breakfast · 1 square (about 3 by 3 inches)
items.body: A Jewish holiday favorite: egg noodles baked in a sweet, creamy custard of cottage cheese, sour cream and cream cheese with a cinnamon top.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the dish

items.title: Hot Spinach Artichoke Dip
items.subtitle: snack · about 1/3 cup
items.body: A bubbly, cheesy dip of spinach, artichoke hearts, cream cheese, sour cream, mozzarella and Parmesan.

items.title: Crustless Spinach and Feta Pie
items.subtitle: breakfast,lunch,dinner · 1 wedge
items.body: The flavors of Greek spanakopita (spinach, feta, dill and green onions) baked in an easy egg and cottage cheese custard with no crust.

items.title: Cottage Cheese Pancakes
items.subtitle: breakfast · 3 small pancakes
items.body: Tender, high-protein pancakes made with cottage cheese and eggs. Blend the batter smooth or leave it a little lumpy.

items.title: Lazy Pierogi (Cottage Cheese Dumplings)
items.subtitle: dinner,breakfast · about 12 dumplings
items.body: A Polish family favorite: soft dumplings of cottage cheese, egg and flour, boiled and tossed with butter. Serve them sweet with cinnamon sugar or savory with onions.

items.title: Creamy Cottage Cheese Dill Dip
items.subtitle: snack · about 1/4 cup
items.body: Cottage cheese blended smooth with fresh dill, chives and lemon. A high-protein dip for vegetables and crackers.

items.title: Spinach Lasagna Roll-Ups
items.subtitle: dinner · 2 roll-ups
items.body: Lasagna noodles rolled around a ricotta, spinach and basil filling and baked in marinara under melted mozzarella. Easy to portion.

items.title: Lemon Ricotta Pancakes
items.subtitle: breakfast · 3 pancakes
items.body: Light, moist pancakes with ricotta and fresh lemon zest. Special enough for a weekend, easy enough for a weekday.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the pan

items.title: Spinach and Ricotta Calzones
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 calzone
items.body: Store-bought pizza dough folded around ricotta, mozzarella, spinach and Parmesan, baked golden and served with marinara for dipping.

items.title: Broccoli Alfredo Penne
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Penne and broccoli in a homemade Alfredo sauce of cream, butter, garlic and Parmesan. Add leftover chicken if you like.

items.title: Classic Cream Scones
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 scone
items.body: Tender, lightly sweet scones made with heavy cream. Add dried fruit or chocolate chips if you like.

items.title: Flaky Buttermilk Biscuits
items.subtitle: breakfast,side · 1 biscuit
items.body: Tall, tender Southern-style biscuits from flour, cold butter and buttermilk. Fold the dough a few times for flaky layers.

items.title: Mini Cheesecakes
items.subtitle: snack · 1 mini cheesecake
items.body: Little cheesecakes with a graham cracker crust baked in a muffin tin. Top them with fresh berries.

items.title: Honey-Orange Glazed Bone-In Ham
items.subtitle: dinner · about ⅓ lb as bought (with bone)
items.body: A fully cooked bone-in half ham, scored in diamonds, warmed slowly at 325°F and lacquered with honey, orange and mustard. The bone goes into soup afterward.

ingredients.prep: fully cooked half ham (shank or butt end)

items.title: Garlic and Rosemary Roast Leg of Lamb
items.subtitle: dinner · about 6 oz as bought
items.body: A bone-in leg studded with garlic and rubbed with rosemary, lemon and mustard, roasted at 325°F to a rosy 145°F. Serve with mint sauce.

items.title: Fresh Mint Sauce
items.subtitle: side · about 2 tablespoons
items.body: The bright, sharp British sauce for lamb: chopped mint steeped in sweetened vinegar. Nothing like the green jelly.

items.title: Hard-Cooked Eggs for Dyeing and Eating
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 1 egg
items.body: Firm, evenly set eggs with no green ring, ready to dye, devil or slice. Steaming makes them easier to peel.

items.title: Classic Egg Salad Sandwiches
items.subtitle: lunch · 1 sandwich
items.body: Creamy egg salad with celery and chives on soft bread. A good use for the eggs you dyed and kept in the refrigerator, not the ones that went on the hunt.

items.title: Classic Scalloped Potatoes
items.subtitle: side · about 1 cup
items.body: Thin potato slices baked in a garlicky cream sauce until tender, with a golden top. No cheese: that would make them au gratin.

items.title: Honey Butter Glazed Carrots
items.subtitle: side · about ¾ cup
items.body: Carrots simmered in a little water, then glazed with butter and honey until shiny. Use slim spring carrots with their tops trimmed if you find them.

ingredients.prep: peeled, cut on the diagonal ½ inch thick

items.title: Buttered Peas with Mint
items.subtitle: side · about ½ cup
items.body: Sweet peas warmed with butter, shallot and fresh mint: the classic spring partner for lamb, ready in 15 minutes.

items.title: Strawberry Spinach Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 2 cups
items.body: Baby spinach, sliced strawberries, red onion and crumbled feta with a honey-balsamic dressing. Add toasted almonds if your table eats nuts.

items.title: Hot Cross Buns
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 bun
items.body: Soft spiced buns with raisins and orange zest, marked with a cross and glazed with warm apricot jam. Traditionally eaten on Good Friday.

items.title: Carrot Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
items.subtitle: snack · 1 slice
items.body: A moist, spiced two-layer cake full of grated carrots, with tangy cream cheese frosting. Walnuts are optional.

items.title: Lemon Bars
items.subtitle: snack · 1 bar (2 inches square)
items.body: A buttery shortbread crust under a tart, silky lemon layer, dusted with powdered sugar. Sunny on a spring table.

ingredients.prep: zest of 1, juice of both (about ½ cup)

items.title: Baked Ham and Swiss Sliders
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 2 sliders
items.body: A tray of soft rolls filled with leftover ham and Swiss cheese, brushed with mustard butter and baked until melty. The day-after lunch everyone asks for.

ingredients.prep: or other soft dinner rolls, in one slab
cooked leftover ham, thinly sliced (weighed without the bone)

items.title: Apple Cinnamon Baked Oatmeal
items.subtitle: breakfast · 1 square (about 1 cup)
items.body: A pan of soft, cinnamon-spiced oats with apples, walnuts and raisins. Bake once and reheat all week.

items.title: Apple Pear Crisp
items.subtitle: snack · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Tender apples and pears under a buttery oat and pecan topping. Good warm with a scoop of ice cream.

meta.name: Classic Cheeseburgers
meta.summary: Juicy, simply seasoned burgers that cook on the grill or in a skillet in about 12 minutes.
steps: Divide the beef into 4 equal portions and shape each into a patty about 3/4 inch thick and a little wider than the buns. Press a shallow dimple into the center of each so it stays flat as it cooks. Handle the meat gently.
Wash your hands after shaping. Season both sides of the patties with the salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Heat the grill or a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the patties 4 to 5 minutes per side, flipping once, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Lay a slice of cheese on each patty for the last minute; cover so it melts.
Toast the buns cut side down for 30 to 60 seconds. Move the cooked burgers to a clean plate, not the one that held the raw patties.
Build the burgers with lettuce, tomato and your choice of toppings.
meta.make_ahead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead. Stack them with wax paper between and keep covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze raw patties with wax paper between them for 3 to 4 months for best quality. Thaw overnight in the fridge, or cook from frozen and add a few minutes per side.

leftovers.text: Chop a leftover patty into a quesadilla or over a salad; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Make a few small slider patties (about 2 ounces each) for little hands. They cook in about 3 minutes per side, still to 160°F.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free buns or wrap the burgers in lettuce leaves.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave off the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Cook store-bought veggie patties by the package directions and use the same toppings.

prep_day.ahead: Shape and season the patties; slice the tomato and onion.

steps: Cook the beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 7 minutes. Spoon off extra fat if there is a lot.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomato sauce and water. Simmer 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick enough to hold on a spoon.
Warm the tortillas: wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 30 to 45 seconds, or heat one at a time in a dry skillet.
Set out the filling and toppings so everyone can build their own.
meta.make_ahead: Cook the filling up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F, adding a splash of water.

freezer.text: Freeze the cooked filling flat in a freezer bag for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge overnight.

leftovers.text: Use leftover filling for taco salad, nachos or quesadillas the next day.

meta.kids: Set up a build-your-own bar. Younger children often like the meat, cheese and tortilla separate on the plate.

swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas and this homemade seasoning are naturally free of wheat; check labels on the tortillas.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream; add extra avocado.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans of black or pinto beans, drained and lightly mashed, in place of the beef. Skip the browning step.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the taco filling; shred the lettuce and dice the tomato.

items.title: Classic Meat Lasagna
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Layers of meat sauce, ricotta and mozzarella. Make it on the weekend; it reheats beautifully.

meta.name: Classic Meat Lasagna
meta.summary: Layers of meat sauce, ricotta and mozzarella. Make it on the weekend; it reheats beautifully.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain and lay them flat on an oiled baking sheet so they do not stick.

Meanwhile, cook the beef, sausage and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the meat reaches 160°F, 8 to 10 minutes. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, egg, 1/2 cup Parmesan and parsley.

Spread 1 cup of meat sauce in the baking dish. Layer 4 noodles, half the ricotta mixture, a third of the mozzarella and a third of the remaining sauce. Repeat once. Finish with the last 4 noodles, the rest of the sauce, the rest of the mozzarella and 1/4 cup Parmesan.
Cover with foil (tent it or spray the underside so it does not stick to the cheese). Bake 40 minutes. Uncover and bake 15 to 20 minutes more, until bubbling and the center reaches 165°F.
Let the lasagna rest 15 minutes before cutting so the layers hold together.
meta.make_ahead: Assemble, cover tightly and refrigerate up to 1 day. Add about 15 minutes to the covered baking time, and check that the center reaches 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze assembled, unbaked lasagna wrapped well for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge 1 to 2 days, then bake as directed until 165°F in the center. Baked squares freeze well too.

leftovers.text: Squares reheat well for lunch; microwave covered until 165°F in the center.

meta.kids: Children who are wary of ricotta often like it once it is baked in. Cut small squares for younger kids; it holds heat, so let it cool a few minutes.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free lasagna noodles (cook as the package says) and check the sausage label.
swaps.meatless: Replace the meat with 1 pound chopped mushrooms and 10 ounces thawed, squeezed frozen spinach, browned in a little olive oil.

prep_day.ahead: Make the meat sauce and assemble the whole lasagna; refrigerate or freeze unbaked.

items.title: Spaghetti with Meat Sauce
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: A weeknight meat sauce that simmers while the pasta cooks. Double the sauce and freeze half.

meta.name: Spaghetti with Meat Sauce
meta.summary: A weeknight meat sauce that simmers while the pasta cooks. Double the sauce and freeze half.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most is poured off, so it is left out of nutrition)

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef, onion and carrot and cook, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, sugar, salt, pepper and pepper flakes. Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat and cook 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
While the sauce simmers, bring a large pot of water to a boil with 1 tablespoon salt. Cook the spaghetti until tender, following the package time. Save 1/2 cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the pasta with about half the sauce, adding a little pasta water if it looks dry. Serve the rest of the sauce on top with Parmesan.
meta.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F and cook the pasta fresh.

freezer.text: Freeze the sauce (without pasta) for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Leftover sauce makes quick sloppy joes or a topping for baked potatoes; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Serve some plain buttered noodles on the side with sauce for dipping. Break the spaghetti in half before cooking for easier eating.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free spaghetti.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cups chopped mushrooms and 1 can drained lentils or white beans in place of the beef.

prep_day.ahead: Make a double batch of sauce; refrigerate one, freeze one.

items.title: Pot Roast with Carrots and Potatoes
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: A Sunday-dinner classic you can make in the slow cooker or the oven. The leftovers make great sandwiches.

meta.name: Pot Roast with Carrots and Potatoes
meta.summary: A Sunday-dinner classic you can make in the slow cooker or the oven. The leftovers make great sandwiches.
steps: Pat the roast dry and season all over with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet (or the Dutch oven) over medium-high heat. Brown the roast well on all sides, about 10 minutes total. Browning adds flavor; you can skip it on a busy morning.

Slow cooker: Put the potatoes, carrots, celery and onion in the cooker and set the roast on top. Whisk the tomato paste into the broth with the Worcestershire and pour it over. Add the garlic, thyme and bay leaves. Cover and cook on low 8 to 9 hours or high 5 to 6 hours.
Oven: Heat the oven to 325°F. In the Dutch oven, add the onion, garlic, broth mixture, thyme and bay leaves around the roast. Cover and bake 2 1/2 hours. Add the vegetables and bake 1 hour more.
The roast is safe at 145°F, but chuck becomes fork-tender only after long cooking, when it pulls apart easily. Lift out the meat and vegetables and remove the bay leaves.

For gravy, pour the cooking liquid into a saucepan and bring to a boil. Stir the cornstarch into the water, whisk it in and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until thickened. Slice or pull the beef and serve with the vegetables and gravy.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

meta.make_ahead: Cook a day ahead; chill the meat in its liquid. Lift off the hardened fat, then reheat gently to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze sliced beef in gravy for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Potatoes turn grainy when frozen, so eat those first.

leftovers.text: Pile leftover beef on rolls with a little gravy for hot sandwiches, or use it in beef stew or tacos; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Shred the beef and serve with the soft carrots. Let little ones dip pieces in the gravy.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free Worcestershire sauce and broth (check labels); cornstarch is gluten-free.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables and season the roast the night before; start the slow cooker in the morning.

items.title: Simple Roast Chicken
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: A whole chicken roasted with lemon, garlic and herbs. Leftovers become soup, salads and quesadillas.

meta.name: Simple Roast Chicken
meta.summary: A whole chicken roasted with lemon, garlic and herbs. Leftovers become soup, salads and quesadillas.
equipment: roasting pan or large oven-safe skillet
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Take the chicken out of its package and remove anything in the cavity. Do not rinse the chicken; washing raw poultry spreads germs around the sink. Pat it dry with paper towels and throw them away. Wash your hands and anything the raw chicken touched.
Lay the onion slices in the pan as a rack. Set the chicken on top, breast up.
Mix the butter, salt, pepper, thyme and garlic powder and rub it all over the chicken. Put the lemon halves and garlic cloves inside. Tie the legs together if you like.
Roast 1 hour 10 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer reads 165°F in the thickest part of the breast and the innermost part of the thigh, without touching bone.
Let the chicken rest 15 minutes before carving. Spoon the pan juices over the meat.
Within 2 hours, pull the meat off the leftover carcass and refrigerate it. Save the bones in the freezer for stock if you like.
meta.make_ahead: Rub the chicken with the seasoned butter up to 1 day ahead and keep it uncovered on a plate in the fridge; the skin dries and roasts crisper.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked, pulled chicken in portions for up to 4 months for best quality. Handy for soups, quesadillas and pot pie.

leftovers.text: Use leftover meat in chicken noodle soup, chicken quesadillas, Caesar salad or pot pie; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Many kids like the drumsticks. Pull the meat off the bone for younger children.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Roast a chicken (or two) and pull the meat for the week.

items.title: Family Beef and Bean Chili
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch
items.body: Mild, hearty chili that feeds a crowd and freezes well. Let everyone add heat at the table.

meta.name: Family Beef and Bean Chili
meta.summary: Mild, hearty chili that feeds a crowd and freezes well. Let everyone add heat at the table.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the beef, onion and bell pepper and cook, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 10 minutes. Spoon off extra fat.
Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, oregano, paprika, salt and pepper. Cook 1 minute, stirring.
Stir in the crushed and diced tomatoes, beans, broth and brown sugar. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 30 to 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Taste and add more salt or chili powder if you like. Serve with toppings.
Slow cooker: brown the beef and vegetables first (steps 1 and 2), then put everything in the cooker and cook on low 6 to 8 hours.
meta.make_ahead: Chili tastes even better the next day. Refrigerate up to 4 days and reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Cool, then freeze in meal-size containers for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Spoon over baked potatoes or hot dogs, or fill burritos; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Keep the pot mild and set out hot sauce for grown-ups. Kids like crushing a few tortilla chips on top.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the chili powder and broth labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream.
swaps.meatless: Skip the beef and add 2 more cans of beans plus 1 cup frozen corn.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the whole pot; portion some for lunches and freeze the rest.

items.title: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Tender chicken and crisp vegetables in a simple soy-ginger sauce. Have the rice cooking first.

meta.name: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry
meta.summary: Tender chicken and crisp vegetables in a simple soy-ginger sauce. Have the rice cooking first.
steps: Whisk all the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Add the chicken in one layer, sprinkle with the salt, and cook without stirring 2 minutes, then stir and cook until no longer pink inside and the pieces reach 165°F, about 4 minutes more. Move the chicken to a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil, the broccoli and carrot, and 2 tablespoons water. Cover and cook 2 minutes. Add the bell pepper and snap peas and stir-fry 2 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Return the chicken. Stir the sauce again (the cornstarch settles), pour it in and cook, stirring, until glossy and thick, about 1 minute.
Serve over rice (see Fluffy White Rice), topped with green onions and sesame seeds.
meta.make_ahead: Cut the chicken and vegetables and mix the sauce up to 1 day ahead; keep raw chicken in its own covered container on the bottom shelf.

freezer.text: The vegetables go soft when frozen and reheated. Freeze raw cut chicken instead.

leftovers.text: Pack over rice for lunch; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Serve the sauce on the side for dipping, and let kids pick their vegetables.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free instead of soy sauce, and gluten-free broth.
swaps.meatless: Use 14 ounces firm tofu, pressed and cubed, browned in the oil.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables and chicken (separate containers); mix the sauce; cook the rice.

items.title: Sheet-Pan Sausage and Vegetables
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Smoked sausage roasted with potatoes, peppers and broccoli on one pan. Little to wash.

meta.name: Sheet-Pan Sausage and Vegetables
meta.summary: Smoked sausage roasted with potatoes, peppers and broccoli on one pan. Little to wash.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil or parchment.
Toss the potatoes with 2 tablespoons oil and half the seasonings. Spread on the pan and roast 10 minutes.

Toss the sausage, pepper, onion and broccoli with the remaining oil and seasonings. Add to the pan, spread everything in one layer, and roast 15 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the sausage is browned and steaming hot (165°F).
meta.make_ahead: Cut the vegetables and sausage up to 2 days ahead.

freezer.text: Roasted potatoes do not freeze well.

leftovers.text: Chop leftovers and scramble with eggs for breakfast; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Cut the sausage into half-moons for small children (round coins can be a choking risk).

swaps.gluten_free: Choose a sausage labeled gluten-free.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained chickpeas instead of sausage; add them with the vegetables.

prep_day.ahead: Chop everything and store the vegetables and sausage in one container.

items.title: Glazed Meatloaf
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Tender meatloaf with a sweet tomato glaze. Leftover slices make the best sandwiches.

meta.name: Glazed Meatloaf
meta.summary: Tender meatloaf with a sweet tomato glaze. Leftover slices make the best sandwiches.
equipment: 9-by-5-inch loaf pan or rimmed baking sheet
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. In a large bowl, stir the breadcrumbs into the milk and let them soak 5 minutes.
Add the eggs, 1/4 cup ketchup, Worcestershire, salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, onion and garlic and mix well. Add the beef and mix gently with your hands just until combined. Wash your hands.
Shape into a loaf about 9 by 5 inches on a lined baking sheet (it browns better than in a pan), or press into the loaf pan.
Stir the glaze ingredients together and spread half over the loaf.
Bake 45 minutes. Spread on the rest of the glaze and bake 10 to 20 minutes more, until a thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
meta.make_ahead: Shape the loaf, cover and refrigerate up to 1 day before baking; add about 10 minutes to the time.

freezer.text: Freeze baked slices separated with wax paper for 2 to 3 months, or the raw shaped loaf for 3 to 4 months, for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Cold or warmed meatloaf on bread with ketchup is a lunchbox favorite; reheat to 165°F if serving warm.

meta.kids: Bake some of the mixture in muffin tins (about 20 minutes, still to 160°F) for kid-size mini loaves.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 3/4 cup quick oats labeled gluten-free instead of breadcrumbs, and gluten-free Worcestershire.
swaps.dairy_free: Use water or unsweetened plant milk instead of milk.

prep_day.ahead: Mix and shape the meatloaf; refrigerate covered until baking night.

items.title: Cheesy Baked Ziti
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Pasta baked in marinara with ricotta and a blanket of mozzarella. Add browned meat if you like.

meta.name: Cheesy Baked Ziti
meta.summary: Pasta baked in marinara with ricotta and a blanket of mozzarella. Add browned meat if you like.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most is poured off, so it is left out of nutrition)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water for 2 minutes less than the package time. Drain.
If using sausage, brown it in a skillet, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Stir it into the sauce.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, egg, half the Parmesan, Italian seasoning and pepper.

Toss the pasta with 1 1/2 jars of sauce. Spread half in the baking dish, dot with the ricotta mixture and sprinkle with half the mozzarella. Top with the rest of the pasta, the remaining sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake 20 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until bubbling and 165°F in the center.
meta.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead, cover and refrigerate; add 10 to 15 minutes to the covered time and check for 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze unbaked in a foil pan, well wrapped, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge and bake as directed.

leftovers.text: Reheat portions covered in the microwave to 165°F for lunches.

meta.kids: Mix a portion without ricotta for picky eaters; it bakes the same.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta and check the sauce label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the ricotta and Parmesan, and use a dairy-free shredded cheese.

prep_day.ahead: Assemble the ziti and refrigerate or freeze it unbaked.

items.title: Chicken Noodle Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch
items.body: A comforting pot of soup with tender chicken, carrots and egg noodles.

meta.name: Chicken Noodle Soup
meta.summary: A comforting pot of soup with tender chicken, carrots and egg noodles.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 to 8 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the broth, chicken, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot. Remove the bay leaf.
Bring the soup back to a boil, add the noodles and cook until tender, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the parsley and taste for salt.
meta.make_ahead: Make the soup base (without noodles) up to 4 days ahead. Reheat to a boil and cook the noodles in it just before serving, so they do not go mushy.

freezer.text: Freeze the soup without noodles for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Add fresh noodles when reheating.

leftovers.text: Pack hot soup in a preheated insulated food jar for school lunch: fill the jar with boiling water for a few minutes, empty it, then add soup heated to 165°F.

meta.kids: Use small noodles or broken spaghetti for little spoons.

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice or gluten-free noodles and gluten-free broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.
swaps.meatless: Use vegetable broth and 2 cans drained white beans in place of the chicken.

prep_day.ahead: Make the soup base; cook noodles when serving.

items.title: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner
items.body: A creamy tomato soup from pantry cans and golden grilled cheese for dipping.

meta.name: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
meta.summary: A creamy tomato soup from pantry cans and golden grilled cheese for dipping.
steps: Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, broth, sugar, basil, salt and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender (or carefully in a blender, filled no more than halfway with the lid vented). Stir in the half-and-half and warm through without boiling.
Butter one side of each bread slice. Put 4 slices butter side down in a skillet over medium-low heat, add 2 slices cheese each, and top with the other bread, butter side up.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts. Cut and serve with the soup.
meta.make_ahead: The soup keeps 4 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the soup before adding the half-and-half for 2 to 3 months for best quality; stir it in when reheating.

leftovers.text: Leftover soup makes a quick sauce for pasta.

meta.kids: Cut sandwiches into strips for dipping.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread and broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil in the soup and skip the half-and-half (or use canned coconut milk); use dairy-free cheese and spread.

prep_day.ahead: Make the soup.

items.title: Breakfast-for-Dinner Sheet-Pan Hash
items.subtitle: dinner,breakfast
items.body: Crispy potatoes, sausage and peppers on one pan, topped with eggs. Breakfast for dinner is a weeknight win.

meta.name: Breakfast-for-Dinner Sheet-Pan Hash
meta.summary: Crispy potatoes, sausage and peppers on one pan, topped with eggs. Breakfast for dinner is a weeknight win.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes, bell pepper and onion with the oil, salt, paprika and pepper on a rimmed baking sheet. Roast 25 minutes, stirring once, until browned.
Meanwhile, brown the sausage in a skillet, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Drain on a paper towel.

Scatter the sausage over the potatoes. Make 8 small wells and crack an egg into each. Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are firm. (USDA advises cooking eggs until the yolks and whites are firm.)
Sprinkle with cheese and green onions and serve.
meta.make_ahead: Cube the potatoes and keep them covered in water in the fridge up to 1 day; drain and pat dry before roasting.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Wrap leftover hash and egg in a tortilla for a breakfast burrito; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Scramble the eggs separately for kids who do not like them baked.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the sausage label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Skip the sausage and add 1 can drained black beans with the eggs.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the sausage; chop the peppers and onion.

items.title: Freezer Bean and Cheese Burritos
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner
items.body: A big batch of burritos to wrap and freeze for fast lunches and busy nights.

meta.name: Freezer Bean and Cheese Burritos
meta.summary: A big batch of burritos to wrap and freeze for fast lunches and busy nights.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 4 minutes. Stir in the refried beans, black beans, salsa, cumin, chili powder and salt and heat until steaming, 3 to 4 minutes. Let cool 10 minutes.
Warm the tortillas briefly so they fold without cracking.
Spread about 1/2 cup bean mixture and 1/4 cup rice down the center of each tortilla and top with 1/4 cup cheese. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
To eat now, toast seam side down in a skillet until golden. To freeze, wrap each burrito in foil or plastic and freeze in a bag.
From frozen: unwrap, wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 2 to 3 minutes, turning halfway, until 165°F in the center. Or bake wrapped in foil at 375°F for 35 to 40 minutes.
meta.make_ahead: The filling keeps 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze wrapped burritos for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

meta.kids: Make a few smaller burritos in 8-inch tortillas for little appetites.

swaps.gluten_free: Use large corn or gluten-free tortillas (they crack more easily; warm them well).
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free cheese or skip it and add diced avocado when serving.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the rice and filling, roll the burritos and freeze.

items.title: Chicken Quesadillas
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner
items.body: Crisp tortillas with melted cheese and chicken. A great way to use leftover roast or rotisserie chicken.

meta.name: Chicken Quesadillas
meta.summary: Crisp tortillas with melted cheese and chicken. A great way to use leftover roast or rotisserie chicken.
steps: Toss the chicken with the cumin, chili powder and salt.
Lay a tortilla flat and sprinkle half of it with 1/4 cup cheese, 1/2 cup chicken and another 1/4 cup cheese. Fold over. Repeat with the rest.
Brush a skillet lightly with oil and heat over medium. Cook quesadillas 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts and the filling is hot (165°F for cooked chicken).
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa and sour cream.
meta.make_ahead: Shred the chicken and mix the seasoning up to 3 days ahead (within 3 to 4 days of when the chicken was cooked).

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Cold wedges are fine in a lunchbox with an ice pack.

meta.kids: Cheese-only quesadillas are a good starting point; add a few beans or corn as they get adventurous.

swaps.gluten_free: Use corn tortillas (make smaller ones) and check the rotisserie chicken label.
swaps.meatless: Use 1 can drained black beans and 1 cup corn instead of chicken.

prep_day.ahead: Shred and season the chicken.

items.title: Vegetable Fried Rice
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch
items.body: Day-old rice, eggs and frozen vegetables become dinner in 20 minutes. Add leftover ham or chicken if you have it.

meta.name: Vegetable Fried Rice
meta.summary: Day-old rice, eggs and frozen vegetables become dinner in 20 minutes. Add leftover ham or chicken if you have it.

ingredients.prep: cooked a day ahead and chilled (makes about 4 cups)

steps: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the eggs and scramble until no liquid egg remains (egg dishes are done at 160°F). Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and turn the heat to medium-high. Cook the onion 3 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the peas and carrots (and ham, if using) and cook 2 minutes.
Add the rice, breaking up clumps, and cook without stirring 1 minute so it crisps a little, then stir. Repeat a few times until the rice is hot, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, pepper, eggs and green onions.
meta.make_ahead: Cook the rice a day ahead. Spread hot rice on a tray to cool quickly and refrigerate it within 2 hours.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled fried rice in portions for up to 1 month for best quality; reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Pack for lunch and reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Kids can help crack and beat the eggs and stir in the peas.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free.
swaps.meatless: It is already meatless without the ham.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a big pot of rice for the week; cool quickly and refrigerate.

items.title: Lemon-Garlic Baked Salmon
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Salmon fillets baked with butter, lemon and garlic in about 15 minutes.

meta.name: Lemon-Garlic Baked Salmon
meta.summary: Salmon fillets baked with butter, lemon and garlic in about 15 minutes.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with foil or parchment and set the fillets skin side down on it.
Mix the melted butter, lemon juice and garlic and brush over the salmon. Sprinkle with salt, pepper and paprika.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 145°F and the flesh flakes easily with a fork.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
meta.make_ahead: Mix the lemon-garlic butter up to 3 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze raw fillets instead; thaw overnight in the fridge before baking.

leftovers.text: Flake cold salmon onto a salad or into a wrap the next day.

meta.kids: Check for pin bones by running a finger along the fillet before baking. A drizzle of honey on a kid portion helps (not for babies under 12 months).

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Thaw fillets in the fridge; mix the butter.

items.title: Skillet Pork Chops
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Golden, juicy boneless chops with a quick pan sauce.

meta.name: Skillet Pork Chops
meta.summary: Golden, juicy boneless chops with a quick pan sauce.
steps: Pat the chops dry. Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika and rub on both sides.
Heat the oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chops 4 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F.
Move the chops to a clean plate and let them rest at least 3 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the broth, mustard and honey to the pan and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes, then swirl in the butter. Spoon over the chops.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

meta.make_ahead: Season the chops up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate covered.

freezer.text: Freeze raw chops instead, 4 to 6 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Slice thin for sandwiches or fried rice; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Slice the chop into thin strips for younger children; 145°F pork can look slightly pink in the center and is safe after the rest.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the butter in the sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Season the chops.

items.title: Shepherd's Pie
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Savory beef and vegetables under a mashed-potato crust. Made with beef it is often called cottage pie; use ground lamb for the classic.

meta.name: Shepherd's Pie
meta.summary: Savory beef and vegetables under a mashed-potato crust. Made with beef it is often called cottage pie; use ground lamb for the classic.
steps: Cover the potatoes with cold salted water in a large pot, bring to a boil and cook 15 minutes, until very tender. Drain and mash with the butter, milk and salt.

Meanwhile, heat the oven to 400°F. Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the beef, onion and carrots, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic for 1 minute.

Stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook 1 minute. Add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme, salt and pepper and simmer 5 minutes, until thick. Stir in the peas and corn. (Move to a baking dish if your skillet is not oven-safe.)
Spread the mashed potatoes over the filling to the edges and rough up the top with a fork. Sprinkle with cheese if you like.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbling at the edges, golden on top and 165°F in the center.
meta.make_ahead: Assemble, cool, cover and refrigerate up to 1 day. Bake about 15 minutes longer, until 165°F in the center.

freezer.text: Freeze assembled and unbaked, well wrapped, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge before baking.

leftovers.text: Reheat portions covered to 165°F for lunch.

meta.kids: Kids can help spread and swirl the potatoes.

swaps.gluten_free: Thicken with 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons cold water instead of flour; check the Worcestershire and broth labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Mash the potatoes with olive oil and some of their cooking water; skip the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained lentils and 8 ounces chopped mushrooms instead of beef, with vegetable broth.

prep_day.ahead: Make the filling and mashed potatoes; assemble and refrigerate.

items.title: Hearty Beef Stew
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Chunks of beef simmered with potatoes and carrots until spoon-tender.

meta.name: Hearty Beef Stew
meta.summary: Chunks of beef simmered with potatoes and carrots until spoon-tender.
equipment: Dutch oven or large heavy pot (or slow cooker)
steps: Pat the beef dry, season with the salt and pepper, and toss with the flour.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in two batches, 5 to 6 minutes per batch, adding the last of the oil as needed. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion 4 minutes, then the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme and bay leaves, scraping up the browned bits. Return the beef. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently 1 1/2 hours.

Add the potatoes, carrots and celery and simmer covered 30 to 40 minutes more, until the beef and vegetables are tender. (Beef is safe at 145°F; stew meat needs this long, gentle simmer to turn tender.) Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes. Remove the bay leaves.
Slow cooker: after browning, put everything except the peas in the cooker and cook on low 8 hours. Stir in the peas at the end.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

meta.make_ahead: Stew is even better the next day. Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Potatoes soften a little after freezing.

leftovers.text: Pack in a preheated insulated food jar for lunch; reheat to 165°F first.

meta.kids: Cut the meat and vegetables a little smaller for young children.

swaps.gluten_free: Toss the beef in 2 tablespoons cornstarch instead of flour; check the broth and Worcestershire labels.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the stew start to finish; it reheats well all week.

items.title: Chicken Pot Pie
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Creamy chicken and vegetables under a flaky crust. Uses leftover or rotisserie chicken.

meta.name: Chicken Pot Pie
meta.summary: Creamy chicken and vegetables under a flaky crust. Uses leftover or rotisserie chicken.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a baking sheet on the lower rack to catch drips.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and celery 5 minutes. Stir in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the broth, then the milk. Simmer, stirring, until thick, about 3 minutes. Add the thyme, salt, pepper, chicken and peas and carrots.
Line the pie plate with one crust, pour in the filling and top with the second crust. Pinch the edges to seal, cut 4 small slits in the top and brush with the egg.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the filling bubbles and reaches 165°F. Let it rest 10 minutes before cutting.
meta.make_ahead: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Assemble with cold filling and add 10 minutes to the baking time.

freezer.text: Freeze unbaked, well wrapped, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Bake from frozen at 400°F for about 60 to 70 minutes (cover the edges with foil if they brown too fast) until 165°F in the center.

leftovers.text: Reheat wedges in the oven or microwave to 165°F.

meta.kids: Kids can cut shapes from crust scraps to decorate the top.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free crust and thicken with 3 tablespoons cornstarch mixed into the cold milk.
swaps.meatless: Use 3 cups mixed vegetables and 1 can drained white beans instead of chicken, with vegetable broth.

prep_day.ahead: Make the filling; assemble on the night you bake.

items.title: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch,side
items.body: A smooth, creamy cheese sauce made in the same pot as the pasta.

meta.name: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
meta.summary: A smooth, creamy cheese sauce made in the same pot as the pasta.

steps: Cook the macaroni in a large pot of boiling salted water until just tender. Drain and set aside.

Slowly whisk in the milk. Cook, whisking, until it thickens and coats a spoon, 4 to 5 minutes. Stir in the mustard, garlic powder and salt.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cheese a handful at a time until smooth. Add the macaroni and stir to coat.
meta.make_ahead: Best fresh. To reheat, add a splash of milk and warm gently, stirring, until hot (165°F).

freezer.text: Freeze portions for up to 2 months for best quality; the sauce may separate a little, so stir in milk while reheating.

leftovers.text: Spoon into a preheated insulated food jar for lunch.

meta.kids: Stir in a cup of frozen peas or steamed broccoli with the pasta for extra vegetables.

items.title: Slow Cooker BBQ Pulled Pork
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch
items.body: Pork shoulder cooked low and slow, shredded and tossed with barbecue sauce. Feeds a crowd or a week of lunches.

meta.name: Slow Cooker BBQ Pulled Pork
meta.summary: Pork shoulder cooked low and slow, shredded and tossed with barbecue sauce. Feeds a crowd or a week of lunches.
steps: Mix the rub ingredients and rub all over the pork.
Lay the onion in the slow cooker, set the pork on top, and pour the broth and vinegar around it.
Cover and cook on low 8 to 10 hours (or high 5 to 6), until the pork pulls apart easily with a fork. It is safe at 145°F, but shoulder needs long cooking to become tender enough to shred.
Lift out the pork, shred it with two forks and discard any large pieces of fat. Skim the fat from the juices.
Return the meat to the cooker with 1 cup of the juices and the barbecue sauce. Stir and keep warm. Serve on buns with coleslaw.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

meta.make_ahead: Cook up to 4 days ahead; reheat to 165°F with a splash of the juices.

freezer.text: Freeze shredded pork with some juices for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

meta.kids: Toss a portion with less sauce for kids who like it mild.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika and Italian seasoning.
Toss the potatoes and carrots with 2 tablespoons oil and half the seasoning and spread on the baking sheet.
Pat the chicken dry (do not rinse it), rub with the rest of the oil and seasoning, and set skin side up on the vegetables. Wash your hands.
Roast 35 to 45 minutes, until the skin is crisp and a thermometer in the thickest thigh, not touching bone, reads 165°F. Thighs stay juicy even if they go a bit higher.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix the chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
In a large bowl toss the chicken, peppers and onion with the oil and spices. Spread in one layer on the baking sheet (use two pans if crowded). Wash your hands and the bowl.
Roast 18 to 22 minutes, stirring once, until the vegetables are tender and the chicken is no longer pink inside and reaches 165°F.

meta.name: Lentil Vegetable Soup

meta.name: Sheet-Pan Pizza Night
meta.summary: One big pizza on a baking sheet, with half plain cheese and half toppings so everyone is happy.
steps: Let the thawed dough sit covered at room temperature 30 minutes so it stretches easily (or thaw in the fridge overnight, then do this).
Heat the oven to 450°F. Oil the baking sheet with 1 tablespoon oil. Press and stretch the dough to fill the pan; if it springs back, rest it 5 minutes and try again. Brush with the remaining oil.
Spread the sauce to within 1/2 inch of the edges and sprinkle with Italian seasoning, then mozzarella. Add toppings to half or all.
Bake on the lowest rack 15 to 20 minutes, until the crust is golden underneath and the cheese bubbles. Cool 5 minutes and cut into squares.

meta.name: Crispy Baked Fish Tacos
meta.summary: Panko-coated white fish baked until crisp, with a quick lime slaw.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and oil the baking sheet.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and the fish flakes easily and reaches 145°F.

Fill warm tortillas with fish, slaw and toppings.

meta.summary: Tall, tender pancakes from scratch. Make extra and freeze them for school mornings.

steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla. Pour into the dry ingredients and stir just until no dry flour shows; small lumps are fine.

Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat and brush with butter. Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form on top and the edges look dry, 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until golden.
Keep cooked pancakes warm on a baking sheet in a 200°F oven while you finish the rest.

steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper until no streaks of white remain.

Push the eggs slowly from the edges to the center with a spatula, making large soft curds. Keep going until no liquid egg remains, 3 to 5 minutes (egg dishes are done at 160°F). Stir in cheese at the end if you like.
Serve right away with toast.
